threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know you’re new if you still hesitate at the bus stop when the ‘W’ on the timetable stands for ‘Wait’ and not ‘Wandsworth’.
Last night on the 59, a chap serenaded the whole bus with 80s ballads. We all rolled our eyes but ended up clapping at his grand finale by Vauxhall.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a street artist painting a mural of a pigeon on a wall, while a kid next to him was feeding real pigeons. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a late-night döner while listening to impromptu DJ sets at the corner of Oranienstraße. It's chaos and magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their irritation at tourists taking photos in front of the murals but ignoring the smell of fresh tamales just steps away.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading waiting passengers at the Powell station with a ukulele. Perfectly off-key but somehow made the delay feel like a moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about trendy shops, but they miss the tiny bakeries tucked away on quiet streets where locals grab their morning pastries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their struggle with the metro map; they still check for stops like it’s an ancient scroll.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still cringe when the bus driver calls you 'darling'—the locals consider it standard fare. Embrace it, or you'll stand out.
Heard a guy on the 3 bus last night ranting about how the tube strike ruined his plans to find the best jollof rice in SE24. He had a whole list.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy in a full tuxedo buying a döner at 3 AM near Hermannplatz. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a random open-air gallery in the middle of a parking lot, showcasing local artists' work while people grab a döner next door.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their instinct to avoid BART delays; they won't even sweat it when a train’s brakes are on the fritz. It's a daily hustle.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a tourist tried to pay with a donut in the Muni bus. Driver just shrugged, took it, and smiled. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but they're missing the real magic in the tiny bars that serve homemade vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they approach the metro ticket machines, fumbling with coins like they’re encrypting a treasure map.
